specification: Epic: Widget names are case- and whitespace-insensitive: the store keeps each name normalised (trimmed, lower-case), and a client can always look a widget up by the name it created it with, in any case or spacing. Widgets record their creation time.

findings.Message: The epic requires a client to look a widget up by the name it created it with in any case or spacing, but FindByName compares the raw input ordinally, so FindByName("ALPHA") or FindByName("  Alpha ") returns null; the input must be normalised the same way Add normalises names.
The new by-name route passes the raw path value straight to FindByName, so it inherits the case- and whitespace-sensitive lookup and returns 404 for mixed-case or padded names the client created.

This test locks in case-sensitive lookup (FindByName("ALPHA") returns null), which contradicts the epic's requirement that lookup works in any case, so it asserts the wrong behaviour and must be changed with the implementation.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: Widget gained a required third parameter, and the plan itself notes that other two-argument new Widget(...) call sites (e.g. IntegrationTests/WidgetRepositoryTests.cs) were not checked, so the solution may fail to compile.

FindByName does not normalise its input, so a client that created a widget as "Alpha" or "  Alpha " gets null from the stored lower-case name, which violates the ticket's requirement that lookup works in any case or spacing.
The test locks in case-sensitive lookup, which contradicts the ticket's requirement that a widget can be found by its creation name in any case, so it would enforce the wrong behaviour.

findings.Snippet:
app.MapGet("/widgets/by-name/{name}", (string name, WidgetStore store) =>
    store.FindByName(name) is { } widget ? Results.Ok(widget) : Results.NotFound());
findings.Message: The route passes the raw path segment straight to FindByName without normalisation, so requests using different casing or surrounding whitespace return 404 instead of the widget.

FindByName neither trims nor lower-cases the query, so a client cannot find a widget by the name it created it with in any case or spacing (e.g. FindByName("ALPHA") or FindByName("  Alpha ") returns null), which the ticket requires.
This test locks in the case-sensitive lookup behaviour that contradicts the ticket, and no test covers lookup by a mixed-case or padded name.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: The two-argument Widget constructor was removed; the plan states other new Widget(...) call sites (e.g. IntegrationTests/WidgetRepositoryTests.cs) were not checked and may no longer compile.

FindByName compares the raw input against the stored normalised name with an ordinal, case-sensitive match and no trimming, so a client cannot look a widget up by the name it created it with in any case or spacing (e.g. Add("  Alpha ") then FindByName("  Alpha ") or FindByName("Alpha") returns null), which the epic requires.
The test enshrines case-sensitive lookup by asserting FindByName("ALPHA") returns null, which contradicts the epic and would block the required behaviour from being correct.
The by-name route passes the raw path segment straight to FindByName without normalising it, so lookups by mixed-case or padded names return 404 instead of the widget.
